tasks.title: Lecture #79
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
tasks.transcript:
Cognitive dissonance refers to the mental discomfort experienced when a person holds two or more contradictory beliefs, values or attitudes simultaneously. This theory, developed by psychologist Leon Festinger in the 1950s, suggests that people are motivated to reduce this discomfort by changing their attitudes, beliefs or behaviors. For example, imagine someone who values health but smokes cigarettes. The conflict between their behavior smoking and their belief valuing health creates cognitive dissonance. To reduce this discomfort, they might decide to quit smoking or rationalize their behavior by downplaying the health risks associated with smoking.
Cognitive dissonance can also play a significant role in decision making. When faced with a difficult choice, people often experience dissonance after making a decision, particularly if the chosen option has downsides. To alleviate this discomfort, they may seek out information that supports their choice and ignore information that contradicts it.
Understanding cognitive dissonance is crucial for psychologists because it explains various aspects of human behavior, including why people sometimes act in ways that contradict their stated beliefs and values. Next, we will discuss some experiments conducted to study cognitive dissonance and their implications for psychological research.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.B: How people react when they experience a contradiction
options.C: How people should resolve conflicts with other people
options.D: How a psychological theory has been developed

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：这段谈话的主要话题是什么？ 定位原文：Cognitive dissonance refers to the mental discomfort experienced when a person holds two or more contradictory beliefs, values or attitudes simultaneously. （全文围绕 cognitive dissonance 的定义、例子、在决策中的作用以及重要性展开） 选项分析： A. How people make difficult choices 人们如何做出艰难选择。谈话中提到 decision making，但这是 cognitive dissonance 的一个应用方面，不是主要内容，所以A选项错误。 B. How people react when they experience a contradiction 人们在经历矛盾时如何反应。cognitive dissonance 正是描述这种矛盾带来的不适以及人们如何减少这种不适，所以B选项正确。 C. How people should resolve conflicts with other people 人们应该如何解决与他人的冲突。谈话中未涉及与他人冲突，所以C选项错误。 D. How a psychological theory has been developed 一种心理学理论是如何发展的。谈话中提到理论由 Festinger 在1950年代提出，但未详细讲述发展过程，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention someone who smokes cigarettes?

options.A: To explain the health risks of smoking
options.B: To illustrate a case of cognitive dissonance
options.C: To point out a way of improving a decision-making process
options.D: To identify a result of a psychological experiment in the 1950s

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：说话者为什么提到吸烟的人？ 定位原文：For example, imagine someone who values health but smokes cigarettes. The conflict between their behavior smoking and their belief valuing health creates cognitive dissonance. 选项分析： A. To explain the health risks of smoking 解释吸烟的健康风险。例子中提到健康风险，但这是为了说明矛盾，而不是解释风险本身，所以A选项错误。 B. To illustrate a case of cognitive dissonance 举例说明认知失调的一个案例。说话者用这个例子说明持有矛盾信念/行为时产生的不适，所以B选项正确。 C. To point out a way of improving a decision-making process 指出改进决策过程的方法。例子与决策过程无关，所以C选项错误。 D. To identify a result of a psychological experiment in the 1950s 指出1950年代一个心理学实验的结果。说话者未提到这是实验结果，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what do people sometimes do after making a decision?

options.A: Focus on the downsides of the decision
options.B: Change their decision-making strategy for future decisions
options.C: Seek the advice of a psychologist
options.D: Search only for information that only supports the decision

questions.analysis: 答案：D 题目问的是：根据说话者，人们在做出决定后有时会做什么？ 定位原文：To alleviate this discomfort, they may seek out information that supports their choice and ignore information that contradicts it. 选项分析： A. Focus on the downsides of the decision 关注决定的缺点。说话者说人们会忽略矛盾信息，而非关注缺点，所以A选项错误。 B. Change their decision-making strategy for future decisions 为未来的决定改变决策策略。谈话中未提及，所以B选项错误。 C. Seek the advice of a psychologist 寻求心理学家的建议。谈话中未提及，所以C选项错误。 D. Search only for information that only supports the decision 只寻找支持该决定的信息。说话者明确说 seek out information that supports their choice，所以D选项正确。

questions.stem: What will the speaker most likely discuss next?

options.C: Possible problems with the theory of cognitive dissonance

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：说话者接下来最可能讨论什么？ 定位原文：Next, we will discuss some experiments conducted to study cognitive dissonance and their implications for psychological research. 选项分析： A. Common beliefs about cognitive dissonance 关于认知失调的常见信念。谈话中未明确说接下来要讲这个，所以A选项错误。 B. Experiments related to cognitive dissonance 与认知失调相关的实验。说话者明确说 next 要讨论研究认知失调的实验，所以B选项正确。 C. Possible problems with the theory of cognitive dissonance 认知失调理论可能存在的问题。谈话中未提及，所以C选项错误。 D. Methods of reducing cognitive dissonance 减少认知失调的方法。谈话中已举例（戒烟或合理化），未说接下来要讲方法，所以D选项错误。
